correctness.rationale: The claim is about ordinary geometric orbits of the no-cyclic-triple vertex complex under all 16 symmetries, and asserts homotopy type, not homeomorphism. In a subdivision chain the vertices have distinct ranks; two points in one closed simplex identified by a symmetry must have the same support and barycentric coefficients. The orbit cells therefore have the signed face-deletion boundaries used in the computation. An independent exact enumeration reproduced 130 nonempty faces, cell counts (15,81,183,177,60), boundary-square zero, and 257 integral unit-pivot chain cancellations leaving ranks (1,0,0,1,0) with zero differential. Splitting off unit pivots removes contractible chain summands and detects integral torsion; it is not a topological collapse. Simple connectivity of the input also follows directly: its 1-skeleton is complete, every missing triangle {i,i+1,i+2} has its boundary filled by coning it to i+4 modulo 8, and these triangular loops normally generate the relations needed to make the complete graph simply connected. Every even-axis reflection fixes a vertex and every odd-axis reflection fixes an adjacent-edge midpoint. These reflections generate the group, so Armstrong's theorem gives trivial orbit fundamental group. Hurewicz yields a generator represented by a map from S^3, and homological Whitehead upgrades that integral homology isomorphism to a homotopy equivalence of simply connected CW complexes.
residual_risks: The replay is an exact finite integral chain computation, not formal verification or a proof of simple connectivity by itself. The independent reading of Armstrong's cited paper was access-limited; the standard finite-action theorem is applied with the fixed-point-generating hypothesis checked directly.

value.rationale: A full integral homotopy classification of the ordinary quotient at the natural eight-cycle case resolves information genuinely absent from its known rational quotient and its fixed-set classifications. The computation excludes torsion and gives an orbit-space test case a researcher can reuse; the separate simple-connectivity argument turns that calculation into a complete sphere homotopy classification.
residual_risks: The result is only a homotopy equivalence for n=8. It identifies neither a manifold/homeomorphism type nor a uniform family pattern.
